question_text: A 48-year-old woman comes to the physician because of an increasingly painful swelling behind her right knee for the past 2 months. During this time, she has also had intermittent low-grade fever and she has been more fatigued than usual. She has not had any trauma to the knee. Over the past year, she has had occasional pain in her hands and wrists bilaterally. She has hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She drinks 1–2 glasses of wine daily and occasionally more on weekends. Current medications include enalapril, metformin, and glimepiride. Her mother and older brother have osteoarthritis. She is 165 cm (5 ft 5 in) tall and weighs 68 kg (150 lb); BMI is 25 kg/m2. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows a 3-cm nontender mass in the right popliteal fossa that becomes prominent when the knee is extended. There is mild swelling and redness of her right knee joint. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient is a 48-year-old woman presenting with a painful swelling behind her right knee, a nontender mass in the popliteal fossa, mild swelling and redness of the knee, intermittent low-grade fever, fatigue, and bilateral hand and wrist pain. These symptoms suggest an inflammatory process. The presence of a nontender mass that becomes prominent with knee extension, along with systemic symptoms (fever, fatigue), aligns with rheumatoid arthritis, which is characterized by symmetric polyarthritis and systemic manifestations. The family history of osteoarthritis does not strongly support osteoarthritis as the primary diagnosis, especially given the inflammatory nature of her symptoms. Other options like psoriatic arthritis and systemic lupus erythematosus are less likely due to the absence of skin lesions and the specific joint involvement pattern. A popliteal artery aneurysm is also unlikely given the nontender nature of the mass. Therefore, the most likely diagnosis is rheumatoid arthritis, supported by the patient's clinical presentation and symptomatology.
